mechanism_narrative: The recent strong rebound in workplace mobility, from -40.3% at t-1w to -21.6% at t-0w, following a sharp decline, indicates a return of people to their regular work routines. This will subsequently drive an increase in retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks as more people are out during weekdays.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its average over the last 28 days, despite the observed rebound in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated residential mobility, consistently above 16% in the last two weeks, indicates a preference for staying home, directly suppressing out-of-home activities. A slight recent decrease in residential mobility suggests a shift towards more external activities, leading to a modest increase in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its high trend or increases, while RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility serves as a leading indicator for general urban activity. If transit mobility increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week in the next week, it will signal a broader return to out-of-home activities, boosting retail and recreation mobility over the subsequent two weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not show a corresponding increase over the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and sustained recovery in both workplace and transit station mobility indicates a robust return to daily commuting and urban activity. This combined effect will strongly drive an increase in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks, as more people are out and about.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show sustained increases for two weeks, but RETAIL_REC remains flat or decreases over the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained and deepening negative trend in retail and recreation mobility, from -14.0% at t-3w to -26.0% at t-0w over the past four weeks, indicates a persistent reluctance or inability of the population to engage in these activities, suggesting a continued decline or stagnation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a significant and sustained increase over the next 28 days, reversing the observed trend.

mechanism_narrative: In a winter-to-spring transition regime (February 15th), an increase in parks mobility by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week signals improving weather conditions and a general increase in outdoor activity. This shift will encourage more out-of-home movement, indirectly boosting retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by > 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases as specified, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If grocery and pharmacy mobility remains significantly elevated (above 40%) while workplace mobility shows only a partial recovery (remaining below -10%) over the next two weeks, it indicates a continued prioritization of essential errands over discretionary retail and recreation, leading to sustained low retail activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 40% and WORKPLACES remains below -10% for the next two weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains high and WORKPLACES remains low as specified, but RETAIL_REC shows a significant increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in workplace mobility (e.g., >10 points) coupled with a concurrent week-on-week decrease in residential mobility (e.g., >2 points), if observed in the next week, will immediately translate into a short-term boost for retail and recreation mobility over the subsequent week, as people shift from home to work and other activities.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by > 10 points and RESIDENTIAL decreases by > 2 points week-on-week for the next week
failure_condition: The specified changes in WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL occur, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent week.
